Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: John Fletcher (author, Wikidata Q312444), died 1625; Francis Beaumont (author, Wikidata Q313932), died 1616; Philip Massinger (author, Wikidata Q380291), died 1640; Arnold Glover (editor, Wikidata Q16943829), died 1905. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Fletcher, John, 1579-1625; Beaumont, Francis, 1584-1616; Massinger, Philip, 1583-1640; Glover, Arnold, 1865-1905 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The works of Francis Beaumont and John Fletcher, Cambridge : University Press, 1905-, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/worksoffrancisb02beauuoft. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 86%, 39%, 57% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Philip Massinger, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
